previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman, three weeks status post orthotopic liver transplant for end-stage liver disease due to hepatitis C, was readmitted with fever, chills, and hypoxia. Imaging revealed bilateral pleural effusions and patchy lung opacities concerning for hospital-acquired pneumonia, possibly aspiration-related given her history of swallowing difficulty. She was treated with intravenous Vancomycin and Zosyn, later transitioned to oral Levaquin after clinical improvement and negative cultures. Her tacrolimus level was monitored and adjusted to avoid toxicity. Nutritional support continued via feeding tube alongside a pureed diet under supervision. She remained afebrile, oxygenated on room air, and stable throughout the stay. Physical therapy cleared her for return to extended care, where she will complete antibiotic therapy and continue rehabilitation. She was discharged with clear mental status, ambulating with assistance, and a plan for close transplant follow-up.
